original_text: We run the Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) code \texttt{emcee} \citep{2013PASP..125..306F} to infer the best-fitting parameters and their associated errors.
injected_text: We run the nested sampling code \texttt{emcee} \citep{2013PASP..125..306F} to infer the best-fitting parameters and their associated errors.
rationale: The cited paper (Foreman-Mackey et al. 2013, cite key 2013PASP..125..306F, title 'emcee: The MCMC Hammer') introduces emcee as an affine-invariant Markov Chain Monte Carlo ensemble sampler. Re-categorizing emcee as a 'nested sampling code' is a methodology-class mis-attribution at the Bayesian-sampling-paradigm level — nested sampling (MultiNest, dynesty, ultranest) and MCMC are distinct algorithmic families. Cite key preserved byte-for-byte.
ground_truth_description: Replaced 'Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC)' with 'nested sampling' in the SED-fitting sentence using emcee. emcee is explicitly an MCMC ensemble sampler per Foreman-Mackey et al. 2013.

truth.claim_sentence_verbatim: We run the Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) code \texttt{emcee} \citep{2013PASP..125..306F} to infer the best-fitting parameters and their associated errors.

original_text: we confirm three QGs in the vicinity of \textit{Jekyll \& Hyde}, a pair of massive QG and a dusty star-forming galaxy, at $z=3.71$ and two QGs around SXDS-27434 at $z=4.01$.
injected_text: we confirm three QGs in the vicinity of \textit{Jekyll \& Hyde}, a pair of massive QG and a dusty star-forming galaxy, at $z=3.17$ and two QGs around SXDS-27434 at $z=4.01$.
rationale: Headline-number digit swap in the abstract: the Jekyll & Hyde overdensity redshift z=3.71 (the paper's primary target redshift, mentioned 10+ times in the body — Sec. 1, Table 1, Sec. 5) is mis-quoted in the abstract as z=3.17 (digits 7↔1 swapped, both adjacent in the decimal). Body keeps the correct z=3.71; the abstract_vs_body_match predicate fires on the headline number.
ground_truth_description: Swapped two adjacent digits in the abstract's headline redshift for the Jekyll & Hyde overdensity (z=3.71 → z=3.17). The same overdensity is correctly stated as z=3.71 in Sec. 1 ('confirmation of two overdensities ... at z=3.71') and in Table 1 (z_spec=3.7120 for DD-134=Jekyll).

Body anchors: Sec. 1 Introduction (line 336): 'confirmation of two overdensities of massive QGs at z=3.71 and 4.01'; Sec. 2.1 Targets (sec:target, line 341): 'Jekyll & Hyde pair [z=3.71]'; Sec. 5.2 Comparison with cosmological simulations (line 551): 'overdensity at z=3.71'
truth.quantity_label: redshift z of Jekyll and Hyde QG overdensity (abstract anchored to body in Sec. 1, 2.1, 5.2)

rationale: Sign flip in numerator of the canonical galaxy overdensity definition (Eq. 1). The standard cosmological overdensity is δ = (n − n̄)/n̄ (n̄ baseline, perturbation gives δ ∈ (−1, ∞), with δ=0 at n=n̄). Replacing − with + gives δ = (n + n̄)/n̄ which is structurally similar but algebraically wrong: at n=0 it gives δ=1 (instead of −1); at n=n̄ it gives δ=2 (instead of 0). Wolfram refutes against the canonical identity.
ground_truth_description: Replaced the minus sign with a plus sign in the numerator of the overdensity definition equation, so δ = (n+n̄)/n̄ instead of δ = (n−n̄)/n̄. The canonical definition zeroes at n=n̄; the injected version equals 2 there.

truth.term_role: numerator sign in canonical overdensity definition

After the swap, the prose still talks about COSMOS at z~3.71 but points to fig:densz4, which is the SXDS field at z~4.01 panel. ground_truth_description: Swapped the figure cross-reference target from \ref{fig:dens} (COSMOS @ z~3.71) to \ref{fig:densz4} (SXDS @ z~4.01) in a sentence whose claim describes the COSMOS field. Reader inspecting fig:densz4 sees SXDS data, not COSMOS; the prose claim and the referenced figure no longer match.
